# Test: shared mineral kill-drop rule

Test-first task for AH-0MUHMT5JC004WRSB (AC3, AC5).

## Goal

Write deterministic unit + guard tests that pin the contract of the shared mineral kill-drop rule **before** it is implemented, so `PlayScene` and the gyms provably share one rule.

## Required coverage

- Small asteroid (`getSizeTier() === 'small'`) → exactly one mineral drop at the asteroid's death position.
- Large and medium asteroid → no direct drop (their small split children drop).
- Non-asteroid enemy that absorbed N minerals → re-drops between `mineralRedropFractionMin` and `mineralRedropFractionMax` of N, never more than N, at the death site, using a seeded RNG for determinism.
- Non-asteroid enemy with 0 absorbed minerals → no drops.
- Re-drop scatter stays within `MINERAL_REDROP_SCATTER_RADIUS` of the death site.

## Assumption

Shared helper module path: `src/scenes/core/mineralKillDrops.ts` exporting `resolveMineralKillDrops(scene, entity, rng): Mineral[]` (operator selected the shared-helper approach — see the parent item's Appendix).

## Acceptance Criteria

- **AC3 — Single shared code path.** The mineral kill-drop rule (small-asteroid drop + non-asteroid re-drop) has one production definition that both `PlayScene` and `GymFormationScene` consume, and a repo-wide guard asserts it.
- **AC5 — Tests are added and green.** New tests cover the shared rule and the guard; `npm test` for the new files passes.
- The unit tests are deterministic (seeded RNG, no reliance on `Math.random`) and cover every bullet under Required coverage.
- Tests fail before the implementation task lands and pass once it does.

## Key Files

- `src/scenes/core/mineralKillDrops.test.ts` — new.
- `src/scenes/core/CombatScene.equivalence.test.ts` — extend guard.
- `src/test/duplicateBodyGuard.ts` — shared guard helper (extend if needed).
- `src/entities/__tests__/BaseEnemy.minerals.test.ts` — keep green / extend.

# Wire gyms to the shared mineral kill-drop helper

Implementation task for AH-0MUHMT5JC004WRSB (AC1, AC2, AC3).

## Goal

Make every formation gym (including `GymMinerals` and the `GymEnemies` asteroid row) drop minerals on enemy destruction exactly as the game does, by calling the shared helper.

## Minimal implementation

- In `GymFormationScene`, add an injectable RNG (`protected rng: () => number = Math.random` plus a `setRng()`/config seam) used for mineral drops.
- Add a single `_spawnMineralKillDrops(entity)` path that calls `resolveMineralKillDrops(...)` and registers the returned minerals in the gym's mineral field.
- Call it from both the generic destruction path (`onEnemyDestroyed`) and the EXPLODE button (`explodeRandom`), so every destruction path drops exactly once.
- Keep the existing asteroid-split config seam unchanged (splitting stays scene/config-specific).
- Update the `GymMinerals` / `GymFormationScene` docstrings to describe the shared code path.

## Acceptance Criteria

- **AC1 — Gyms drop on small-asteroid destruction.** Destroying a small asteroid in `GymMinerals` / `GymEnemies` asteroid row spawns exactly one mineral at its position.
- **AC2 — Gyms re-drop for non-asteroid enemies.** In a gym, a non-asteroid enemy re-drops a configured fraction of the absorbed minerals at its death site.
- **AC3 — Single shared code path.** The mineral kill-drop rule (small-asteroid drop + non-asteroid re-drop) has one production definition that both `PlayScene` and `GymFormationScene` consume.
- Large and medium asteroids drop none directly; their small split children do.
- The gym test suites added by the test-first task pass, and `npm test` plus `npm run typecheck` pass.

- `src/scenes/gym/core/GymFormationScene.ts` — `onEnemyDestroyed`, `explodeRandom`, RNG seam, mineral field.

# Boss integration on the shared tick (+ teleport avoidance, minions)

**Parent:** `AH-0MUII2FJ5007MDDA` (register gap 6). **Depends on:** child #1 (player tick).

## Summary

`PlayScene._updateBoss(dt)` advances the boss inside `tick`, before collisions; `GymBoss.update` calls `super.tick(dt)` and *then* advances the boss, so `GymBoss.tick(dt)` never advances the boss and bullet timing/ordering differs. `PlayScene.getAdditionalTeleportBodies()` makes P7 teleport avoid the boss; `GymBoss` does not. `PlayScene._spawnMinions` spawns phase minions; the gym has no equivalent. Move boss advancement onto the shared tick path (via a hook) and align teleport avoidance and minion spawning.

## Acceptance Criteria

- [ ] **AC1** — Boss advancement is a shared hook called from `tick`, so a single `tick(dt)` advances the boss in both `PlayScene` and `GymBoss` with the same ordering relative to collisions. Verified by a cross-scene test asserting boss bullets appear after the same `tick`.
- [ ] **AC2** — P7 teleport avoids the boss in `GymBoss` as in the game (shared `getAdditionalTeleportBodies` behaviour).
- [ ] **AC3** — Phase-minion spawning matches the game (or is an explicitly documented, producer-approved constrained-feature difference). If mirrored, `GymBoss` uses the shared `planMinionSpawns`.
- [ ] **AC4** — No observable game change; all `PlayScene` boss tests and `GymBoss` tests pass.
- [ ] **AC5** — All related documentation is updated, including code comments, `docs/ENEMY_DESIGN_AND_IMPLEMENTATION.md` §3–§5 and the `GymBoss` docstring.
- [ ] **AC6** — Full project test suite must pass with the new changes.


**Parent-AC traceability** (implements parent `AH-0MUII2FJ5007MDDA`):
- [ ] **Parent-AC traceability (AC1)** — [ ] **AC1 — Each gap in the register has a single shared implementation.** Gaps 1–11 are closed by extracting the duplicated behaviour into the shared core/module or by consuming an existing shared hook; no production scene re-implements a shared behaviour. Verified by the extended duplicate-body guard and by prototype-identity assertions.
- [ ] **Parent-AC traceability (AC2)** — [ ] **AC2 — Behavioural gaps are closed (or explicitly documented as intentional).** Every behavioural difference identified in gaps 1–11 (P9 magnet in formation gyms, P4 notice, per-type pickup cues, boss-in-`tick`, boss teleport avoidance, teleport gating, hold overflow, restart effect reset, GymPlayer input) is either made identical to the game or recorded as an intentional, approved difference in the epic description and the relevant child.
- [ ] **Parent-AC traceability (AC3)** — [ ] **AC3 — Cross-scene equivalence for every object.** Automated tests boot both `PlayScene` and each gym and assert identical outcomes for the player, each enemy archetype, asteroids (incl. split), the boss, minerals (collection/hold/choice), power-ups (spawn/lifecycle/collect/magnet/bomb/cues) and projectiles under the same input and `dt`.
- [ ] **Parent-AC traceability (AC5)** — [ ] **AC5 — No behaviour regression in the game.** `PlayScene` behaviour and all existing tests remain green; any change to game behaviour is called out explicitly in the epic and approved as canonical.
- [ ] **Parent-AC traceability (AC6)** — [ ] **AC6 — Documentation.** `docs/Game Design Document.md` §6.4, `docs/ENEMY_DESIGN_AND_IMPLEMENTATION.md`, the gym docstrings and `README.md` describe the shared behaviour modules, the hooks a gym implements, and the constrained-feature (not divergent-code) nature of gyms.
- [ ] **Parent-AC traceability (AC7)** — [ ] **AC7 — Full project test suite passes.** The complete suite (`/skill:test`, `npm test`) passes with zero failures and no newly-flaky tests.

## Key Files

- `src/scenes/core/CombatScene.ts` / `CombatCoreScene.ts` — boss-update hook.
- `src/scenes/PlayScene.ts` — `_updateBoss` delegates.
- `src/scenes/gym/GymBoss.ts` — remove `update` override; implement hooks.
- `src/waves/BossMinions.ts`, `src/entities/Boss.ts` — reused.
- `src/scenes/gym/GymBoss.test.ts`, `src/scenes/PlayScene.*boss*` — coverage.

- **OQ4 (epic):** should `GymBoss` spawn phase minions as the game does, or is that a deliberately constrained gym feature? *Recommended: mirror it (behaviour), possibly behind a toggle.*

# Intake Brief — Make P9 Magnet timed on pickup and permanent-stack on upgrade (AH-0MUTOTLCY005NZ8L)

**Headline:** Bring the **P9 Magnet** into line with the **P10 Mineral Scoop** hybrid model — a **15 s, refresh-only** timed drop-attraction for field pickups and a **permanent stacking (cap 5)** attraction for the hold-full upgrade — implemented once in the shared `EffectsRegistry` so the game and every gym run identical behaviour.

## Problem statement

The P9 Magnet is currently **always** a permanent stack (cap 5): every pickup, whether a field drop or a hold-full reward, permanently increases the attraction radius. The P10 Mineral Scoop (AH-0MUPMR9TX00756BQ) introduced a hybrid model — timed on field pickup, permanent-stacking on upgrade — and the operator requested during that intake that P9 be brought into line for design consistency. Until this change the two attraction power-ups share a radius curve but not the same duration/stacking semantics, which is an inconsistency the player can feel and the docs must paper over.

## Users

- **Player** — wants a predictable, escalating reward loop: a temporary convenience from a field drop, and a permanent, stacking boon from a deliberate hold-full choice.
- **Developer** — wants the magnet's timed/permanent behaviour defined once in the shared `EffectsRegistry` and consumed by every scene, so the game and gyms cannot drift.

Example user stories:

- As a player, when I collect a **P9 Magnet** field drop, nearby drops drift toward my ship for **15 s** so pickups are easier; re-collecting refreshes the timer to full.
- As a player, when I choose P9 as a **hold-full reward**, the drop attraction becomes a permanent part of my run, so I never lose the convenience.
- As a developer, the magnet's timed/permanent behaviour is modelled once in the shared registry and every scene consumes the same effective-stacks accessor, so the game and gyms run identical code.

## Acceptance Criteria

- [ ] **Field pickup is a timed, refreshing effect.** `applyCollect('P9')` (the field-drop path, no `permanent` flag) activates a **15 s** drop-attraction effect; re-collecting refreshes the timer to full and **does not** add permanent stacks. Verified by unit tests in `src/powerups/effects.test.ts` (activation, expiry after 15 s, refresh, no permanent stack).
- [ ] **Hold-full upgrade is a permanent stacking effect.** `applyCollect('P9', true)` (the `applyMineralChoiceReward` path) grants a **permanent** attraction that stacks up to **5** and never decays on `tick`. Verified by unit tests in `src/powerups/effects.test.ts` / `src/powerups/__tests__/effects.permanent.test.ts`.
- [ ] **One shared effective-stacks accessor drives attraction.** A `magnetEffectStacks()` accessor (mirroring the existing `scoopEffectStacks()`) returns the permanent stack count when any upgrade was chosen, otherwise **1** while the timed field pickup is active, otherwise **0**. `CombatCoreScene._applyDropMagnet` consumes it, so `PlayScene` and every gym pull drops with identical range semantics; the repo-wide duplicate-body/equivalence parity guard stays green.
- [ ] **Help copy and documentation reflect the hybrid model.** The `POWER_UP_CATALOGUE.P9` description, GDD §4.4 table/notes and README power-up list describe P9 as "15 s timed pickup / permanent stacking when chosen as a reward (cap 5)", matching the P10 wording style.
- [ ] All related documentation is updated to reflect the changes, including code comments, README, and any relevant wiki or docs site entries.
- [ ] Full project test suite must pass with the new changes.

## Constraints

- **Parity rule (AGENTS.md):** shared behaviour lives once in `src/powerups/` and `src/scenes/core/` and is consumed by both the game and the gyms; no divergent copy. The duplicate-body guard in `src/scenes/core/CombatScene.equivalence.test.ts` and the gym-parity docs assertion must stay green. Only a *disabled* feature may differ.
- **Duration (operator decision, parent intake Q1/Q5):** field pickup is **15 s**, refresh-only.
- **Timed radius (documented assumption):** while only the timed effect is active, use the minimum active radius — the equivalent of **one magnet stack** (`magnetRadius(shipSize, 1)` = `1 × 20 × 1.5` = **30 px** at `SHIP_SIZE = 20`), mirroring the P10 decision. Permanent stacks (≥ 1) define the radius when present. (Non-blocking; see Open questions.)
- **Single radius curve:** `magnetRadius(shipSize, stacks)` remains the one source of truth for both P9 and P10 (`mineralScoopRadius` delegates to it) — do not fork or change its signature/semantics.
- **Cap stays 5:** `P9_MAX_STACKS` remains the permanent-stack cap; the timed path never stacks.
- **No new activation key:** the magnet stays passive.
- **Existing-test ripple:** today many tests call `applyCollect('P9')` (no flag) expecting permanent stacks (`src/ui/HUD.test.ts`, `src/powerups/effects.test.ts`, scene and gym tests). These must be updated to the **permanent** path (`applyCollect('P9', true)`) wherever they intend the upgrade, and the timed path covered by new tests. This is expected work, not a regression.
- **CHANGELOG.md is excluded** (ship skill owns it). Do not include CI/CD pipeline tests.

## Existing state

- `EffectsRegistry` (`src/powerups/effects.ts`) already models the P10 hybrid: `_scoopStacks`, `P10_MAX_STACKS`, `P10_SCOOP_DURATION = 15`, `isScoopActive()`, `scoopEffectStacks()`, and a `MINERAL_SCOOP` case that branches on `permanent`. The P9 `MAGNET` case currently **ignores** `permanent` and always increments `_magnetStacks` (cap `P9_MAX_STACKS`).
- `magnetRadius(shipSize, stacks)` returns `MAGNET_RADIUS_BASE_MULTIPLIER (1) × shipSize × (1 + MAGNET_RADIUS_PER_STACK (0.5) × stacks)`. `mineralScoopRadius` delegates to it.
- `CombatCoreScene._applyDropMagnet` calls `applyDropMagnet(..., getEffectsRegistry().magnetStacks(), dt)` — the permanent-stack count only.
- The hold-full reward path (`applyMineralChoiceReward`, `src/scenes/core/mineralLayer.ts`) calls `effectsRegistry.applyCollect(option.id, true)` for power-up options; the field-drop path (`CombatCoreScene._collectDrop`) calls `applyCollect(dropId)` with no flag.
- `POWER_UP_CATALOGUE.P9` (`src/powerups/types.ts`) has description "Permanently pulls nearby drops toward the ship (stacks up to 5)." and no `duration`; P10 carries `duration: 15` + `maxStacks: 5`.
- `activeEffects()` surfaces P9 permanent stacks as an `xN` row when `_magnetStacks > 0`; timed P10 surfaces from `_timed` plus a stack row (never `x0`). HUD `formatValue` renders `Ns` for timed rows and `xN` for stack rows.
- Existing tests assuming field-pickup permanence include `src/powerups/effects.test.ts` (`P9 Magnet (AC4)`), `src/ui/HUD.test.ts` (HUD AC2), and scene/gym/drop-layer/equivalence tests that collect P9.

## Desired change

Make P9 a hybrid exactly analogous to P10:

- **Registry:** add `P9_MAGNET_DURATION = 15`; branch the `MAGNET` case on `permanent` (permanent → +1 stack capped at 5; field pickup → timed `_timed` entry, refresh-only); add `isMagnetActive()` and `magnetEffectStacks()`; include the timed P9 row and permanent P9 stack row (never `x0`) in `activeEffects()`; reset both states in `reset()`.
- **Scene wiring:** `CombatCoreScene._applyDropMagnet` consumes `magnetEffectStacks()` instead of `magnetStacks()`.
- **Catalogue:** add `duration: 15` to `P9` and rewrite its description to the hybrid wording.
- **Docs:** update GDD §4.4 (P9 row + notes) and README power-up/effects descriptions; remove the "tracked separately" note where it refers to this now-delivered change.
- **Tests:** extend `effects.test.ts` (timed activation/expiry/refresh, permanent stacking/cap, `magnetEffectStacks()`, `activeEffects()` shape, `reset()`), migrate existing field-pickup-as-permanent assertions to the permanent path, and keep parity/HUD/scene tests green.

## Key Files (predicted)

- `src/powerups/effects.ts` — `P9_MAGNET_DURATION`, hybrid `MAGNET` case, `isMagnetActive()`, `magnetEffectStacks()`, `activeEffects()`, `reset()`; doc-comment updates.
- `src/powerups/types.ts` — `P9` catalogue `duration: 15` + hybrid description.
- `src/scenes/core/CombatCoreScene.ts` — `_applyDropMagnet` uses `magnetEffectStacks()`.
- `src/powerups/effects.test.ts` — timed/permanent P9 unit tests (mirroring the P10 block).
- `src/powerups/__tests__/effects.permanent.test.ts` — permanent-path coverage if applicable.
- `src/ui/HUD.test.ts` — migrate P9 stack assertions to the permanent path; add a timed-row case.
- `src/scenes/core/dropLayer.test.ts`, `src/scenes/core/CombatScene.equivalence.test.ts` — effective-stacks pull + parity guard.
- `src/scenes/PlayScene.test.ts`, `src/scenes/gym/core/GymFormationScene.test.ts`, `src/scenes/gym/GymPowerUpsUtility.test.ts` — scene-level P9 semantics/parity.
- `docs/Game Design Document.md` — §4.4 P9 row + notes.
- `README.md` — power-up / shared-effects descriptions.

## Risks and assumptions

- **Assumption:** the timed/permanent split maps cleanly onto the existing `applyCollect(id, permanent)` flag, exactly as it did for P10. *Mitigation:* registry unit tests for both paths before scene wiring.
- **Risk — behavioural change ripples through existing tests.** Many tests use `applyCollect('P9')` to mean "permanent stack". *Mitigation:* systematically migrate those assertions to `applyCollect('P9', true)` and add explicit timed-path tests; the full suite must be green before `in_review`.
- **Risk — HUD dual timed/stacked display.** P9 changes type between pickups and upgrades; a stale `×0` would mislead. *Mitigation:* only surface stacks/remaining when active, mirroring P10's zero-suppression rule; add a HUD test.
- **Risk — parity drift.** If any scene computes its own stacks or radius, gyms diverge. *Mitigation:* one accessor (`magnetEffectStacks()`), shared `_applyDropMagnet`, and the duplicate-body/equivalence guard.
- **Risk — radius-curve coupling with P10.** `magnetRadius` is shared with the scoop; a careless change would alter P10. *Mitigation:* leave `magnetRadius` untouched and reuse it.
- **Assumption:** reusing the existing P9 pickup cue unchanged is acceptable; no new SFX required.
- **Assumption:** a timed P9 field pickup does **not** clear or cancel an existing permanent upgrade (and vice versa); the effective radius is driven by permanent stacks when present. Mirrors P10.
- **Scope-creep risk:** any generic "attractor target predicate" refactor or further P10 changes are out of scope; record extra opportunities as linked work items, not scope.

## Related work

- **AH-0MUPMR9TX00756BQ — Add a mineral scoop power-up** (completed): introduced the P10 hybrid timed-pickup/permanent-upgrade model and the `applyCollect(id, permanent)` pattern this item mirrors. `discovered-from` this item.
- **AH-0MT7VE4SX0005A8V — Add a Magnet power up** (completed): introduced P9.
- **AH-0MUTTAHQ9001T83A — Halve the base attraction radius for P9 Magnet and P10 Mineral Scoop** (completed): set the current `magnetRadius` base; the single curve this item must preserve.
- **AH-0MTCNYWDO007B6CJ — Unit tests: power-up effects, refresh & magnet math** (completed): existing effects/refresh/magnet test suite to extend.
- **AH-0MU8QTS7O006DSAE / AH-0MTV6NZ6A000GPVG — Magnet pull attraction / pull animation** (completed): shared attraction helper and visual pull; unchanged by this item.

## Related work (automated report)

### Related work items
- **AH-0MTCNZX16007ECPS** – Power-up catalogue + effects (P5, P8, P9) (completed)
- **AH-0MUAYB3OU0087H9W** – Collected powerups need some feel (completed)
- **AH-0MT7UX8LE0072MR3** – Add an extra life power up (completed)

### Repository file matches
- `README.md` — matched: many (magnet, timed, permanent, pickup, upgrade, stack, cap, scoop, effects, gym, parity, tests, docs, …)
- `docs/Game Design Document.md` — matched: many (magnet, timed, permanent, pickup, upgrade, stacking, cap, scoop, effects, parity, tests, docs, …)
- `docs/ENEMY_DESIGN_AND_IMPLEMENTATION.md` — matched: many (parity, effects, drops, tests, docs, …)

## Appendix: Clarifying questions & answers

- **No new interview round was required.** The design decision that determines this item's behaviour was already captured during the parent P10 intake: Q1 — "B when picked up in gameplay, A when added as an upgrade (create a work item to change the magnet to behave the same way)." Final accepted answer: field pickup = **timed**, hold-full upgrade = **permanent stacking**. Source: interactive reply recorded in AH-0MUPMR9TX00756BQ (`AH-C0MUQCYKT0000D52H`); the discovered-from work item is this item. The seed context supplied in the description therefore suffices to draft the brief, per the intake skill's "skip the interview when the seed context suffices" rule.
- **Q (implicit) — Timed duration.** Answer: **15 s**, consistent with the A-recorded P10 scoop duration. Source: device description + parent intake Q5. Research: `P10_SCOOP_DURATION = 15` in `src/powerups/effects.ts`.
- **Assumption (non-blocking) — Timed-only attraction radius.** Timed P9 uses **one stack's worth** (`magnetRadius(shipSize, 1)`, 30 px at `SHIP_SIZE = 20`), mirroring the P10 decision, with permanent stacks overriding when present. ## Goal

Implement the continuous, thrust-driven thruster hum as a lightweight Tone.js runtime shim, since baked WAV variants cannot reproduce a pitch/gain-continuous, thrust-coupled loop.

As the game's developer, I want the thruster hum to remain continuous and thrust-driven, so the tuning slider stays audible and the hum stays in lockstep with the flame animation.

- Add a small Tone.js-based runtime shim that owns only the thruster hum; all other cues are baked assets (decision recorded on the parent epic).

# Intake Brief — Design level curves for all power-ups (AH-0MUU2QJE2007JNR6)

**Headline:** Give every power-up (P3–P10) a run-scoped integer **level** backed
by a documented, data-driven curve catalogue and a pure resolver — mirroring the
weapon-levelling system (`weaponLevels.ts`) — so a hold-full choice can
measurably strengthen a power-up the player already owns and the upgrade summary
in the hold-full overlay (AH-0MUU1GOAU007RFVR) can render its deltas.

> **STATUS: PAUSED FOR PRODUCER INPUT.** The core design decisions below are
> genuinely open (per the intake interview contract they must not be invented).
> Three questions are recorded in the work item comments and the item is
> flagged `needsProducerReview`. Intake does **not** advance to
> `intake_complete` until they are answered.

## Problem statement

Power-ups P3–P10 currently have **no level concept**. Each is binary/timed, a
single stored stack, or (for P9/P10) a stack count capped at 5
(`src/powerups/types.ts`, `src/powerups/effects.ts`). Weapons, by contrast,
carry a run-scoped integer level whose effects are resolved by a pure,
data-driven curve catalogue (`src/utils/weaponLevels.ts`). Because power-ups
lack levels, spending a hold-full mineral choice on a power-up the player
already owns cannot measurably strengthen it, and the generic upgrade-summary
mechanism shipped by AH-0MUU1GOAU007RFVR cannot render a power-up delta (its
AC5 is currently "adjusted" precisely for this gap).

## Users

- **Player (progression parity):** "As a player, spending a hold-full choice on
  a power-up I already own should measurably strengthen it, so power-ups scale
  across a run the way weapons do."
- **Player (informed choice):** "As a player, I want the hold-full overlay to
  show what a power-up level-up will change, so I can make an informed build
  choice."
- **Designer/tuner:** "As a designer, I want every power-up's level curve in one
  data-driven catalogue with a written rationale, so balance intent cannot drift
  from the numbers scattered through scenes."
- **Developer:** "As a developer, I want one pure resolver consumed identically
  by the game and every gym, so power-up levels cannot diverge (gym↔game parity)."

## Existing state

- `src/powerups/types.ts` — `POWER_UP_CATALOGUE` (P3–P10) with `type`,
  `duration?`, `maxStacks?`, `livesStart?`, `livesMax?`. No `level`.
- `src/powerups/effects.ts` — `EffectsRegistry` holds all power-up state:
  timed map (P3/P5/P6/P10-timed), `_magnetStacks` (P9, cap 5), `_scoopStacks`
  (P10, cap 5), `_teleportStacks` (P7), `_phaseCharges`/`_phasePermanent` (P6),
  `_lives` (P8, start 3 / cap 5). Constants `P5_SPEED_MULTIPLIER`,
  `P8_LIVES_MAX`, `P9_MAX_STACKS`, `P10_MAX_STACKS`, `P3_SHIELD_DURATION`.
  Attraction radius curve in `magnetRadius()` / `src/powerups/mineralScoop.ts`.
- `src/powerups/choice.ts` — `ChoiceOption { id, name, kind, level?,
  changeSummary?, isNew? }`; `buildChoiceCandidates(pool, { weaponLevels })`
  emits `weapon-level` offers with a summary; power-up upgrade summaries are
  **deferred to this item**. Power-up ownership is not currently tracked.
- `src/utils/weaponLevels.ts` — the precedent: `WEAPON_UPGRADE_SPECS`,
  `curveValue()`, `resolveWeaponAtLevel()`, `summariseWeaponLevelChange()`, the
  exponential-saturation curve `cap − (cap − base)·e^(−k·level)`.
- `src/entities/Player.ts` — `equipWeapon()` increments `_weaponLevels`;
  `getWeaponLevel(s)()`. There is **no** equivalent power-up level store.
- `src/scenes/core/mineralLayer.ts` — `applyMineralChoiceReward()` routes
  weapon/weapon-level options to `equipWeapon(id, true)` and everything else to
  `effectsRegistry.applyCollect(id, true)`.
- GDD §4.4 (power-up table + notes) and §4.4.2 (weapon levelling curve) are the
  design references; §4.4.1 documents the hold-full choice overlay.

## Recommended design model (for producer confirmation)

1. **Data-driven catalogue.** Add `src/powerups/powerUpLevels.ts` holding
   `POWER_UP_LEVEL_SPECS` — one spec per levelled variable per power-up, each
   with `base`, finite `cap`, curve rate `k`, `discrete`, `rationale` and a
   short `label` — reusing the shared `exponential-saturation` curve family
   (extract `curveValue`/`UpgradeCurve` from `weaponLevels.ts` into a shared
   module so there is exactly one curve implementation).
2. **Pure resolver.** `resolvePowerUpAtLevel(powerUpId, level)` returns a
   `PowerUpLevelStats` snapshot (name-matched fields per variable). Pure,
   deterministic, monotonic non-decreasing, clamped to caps.
3. **Level store.** A run-scoped power-up level store alongside weapon levels.
   **Recommended:** every power-up collection increments the level (mirroring
   `equipWeapon()`), and existing stack counters (`_magnetStacks`,
   `_scoopStacks`, teleport stacks, phase charges) are **derived from the level**
   rather than tracked separately, so AC3 is satisfied by unification.
4. **Consumption path.** `EffectsRegistry` reads resolved stats (e.g. duration,
   multiplier, max stacks, radius) from the resolver instead of raw constants;
   the same path is used by `PlayScene` and every gym (parity).
5. **Choice integration.** `buildChoiceCandidates` emits power-up level-up
   offers (with `changeSummary`) for owned power-ups, and ownership context is
   added to `ChoiceContext`; `applyMineralChoiceReward` applies the level-up.
   The display code in `MineralChoiceScene` is already generic (AH-0MUU1GOAU007RFVR).

## Acceptance Criteria (draft — to be finalised once questions are answered)

- **AC1 — Data-driven catalogue.** A documented level-curve catalogue exists
  for **every** power-up P3–P10, comparable to `WEAPON_UPGRADE_SPECS`, with a
  written rationale beside each cap/rate.
- **AC2 — Run-scoped integer level.** Every power-up exposes a run-scoped
  integer level with monotonic, diminishing-returns effects and a finite cap;
  the level persists for the run and resets only on run restart.
- **AC3 — Stack reconciliation.** Existing stack/charge semantics
  (P9/P10 cap 5, P7 stacks, P6 charges, P8 lives cap 5) are explicitly
  reconciled with the level model (recommended: derived from level), with no
  double-counting.
- **AC4 — Pure shared resolver.** `resolvePowerUpAtLevel(powerUpId, level)`
  maps `(powerUpId, level)` to effective stats and is consumed by the same
  shared path in the game and every gym.
- **AC5 — Hold-full integration.** The hold-full choice can offer power-up
  level-ups and the summary/New display (AH-0MUU1GOAU007RFVR) renders their
  deltas with no change to the display code.
- **AC6 — Testing/validation.** Unit + parity tests cover the curve, catalogue
  completeness, resolver monotonicity/caps, level store, and choice integration;
  every test serves a meaningful purpose (TDD preferred).
- **AC7 — Documentation.** All related documentation is updated to reflect the
  changes, including code comments, README, and GDD §4.4 / §4.4.2.
- **AC8 — Full suite.** Full project test suite must pass with the new changes.
  (CI/CD pipeline tests are out of scope.)

## Constraints

- **Gym↔game parity (AGENTS.md):** shared behaviour lives once (power-up level
  module + resolver) and is consumed by `PlayScene` and every gym; no divergent
  copy. The duplicate-body guard in `CombatScene.equivalence.test.ts` applies.
- **Single curve implementation:** reuse/share the weapon curve maths; never
  duplicate `curveValue` logic.
- **Backward compatibility:** extend `ChoiceOption`/`ChoiceContext` with
  optional fields; existing strategies and tests keep compiling.
- **Run-scoped:** no leaderboard impact; levels reset on run restart.
- **Within-epic dependencies:** AH-0MUTOTLCY005NZ8L (P9 hybrid timed/permanent)
  is in progress and changes P9 semantics; AH-0MUUM4MTA0081QSW (P9 docs) is
  open. The level design must be consistent with the hybrid P9/P10 model.

## Desired change

See the recommended design model above. The precise effect of a level on each
power-up (and whether field pickups level up) is the subject of the open
questions and must be confirmed before the catalogue values are authored.

## Key Files (predicted)

- `src/powerups/powerUpLevels.ts` *(new)* — `POWER_UP_LEVEL_SPECS`,
  `resolvePowerUpAtLevel`, `PowerUpLevelStats`.
- `src/utils/curve.ts` *(new, or shared export from `weaponLevels.ts`)* — the
  single exponential-saturation `curveValue` + `UpgradeCurve` shared by weapons
  and power-ups.
- `src/powerups/effects.ts` — consume resolved stats; derive stack/charge state
  from level.
- `src/powerups/types.ts` — level metadata on the catalogue if required.
- `src/entities/Player.ts` *(or a run state holder)* — run-scoped power-up
  level store and accessors.

- **Instant/binary effects (medium):** P4 Bomb (instant, stateless) and P8
  Extra Life (hard life cap 5) have no obvious "level" axis. If a level cannot
  meaningfully change them, they may legitimately stay non-levelled — this is
  open question Q2.
- **Stack double-counting (medium):** levels and existing stack counters must
  not both apply. Mitigation: derive stacks from level (recommended).
- **Balance/feel (medium):** power-up levels affect survivability (shield,
  phase, lives), which is more balance-sensitive than weapon damage; caps must
  be conservative and documented.

  increment its level (mirroring weapons, so field drops also level up), or do
  only hold-full permanent choices increment levels while field pickups keep
  their current timeline/stack behaviour?

  - B. Only hold-full permanent choices level up; field pickups unchanged.
  - C. Levels only for the stackable power-ups (P9/P10); the rest stay binary.

    pickup feel meaningful and reuses the same mental model. **OPEN QUESTION.**

- **Q2 — What a level changes per power-up (and stack reconciliation).** Should
  each power-up expose a small set of levelable variables (magnitude, duration,
  charges/stack cap) resolved by the shared curve, with existing stack counters
  derived from the level — and how should the instant/capped effects be treated?
  - A. Per-power-up variable specs on the shared curve; stacks derived from
    level; P4/P8-levelable only where a meaningful axis exists (else stay flat).
  - B. A single scalar "potency" multiplier applied to each power-up's existing
    effect.
  - C. Only the stack/cap values scale (P9/P10 radius/stacks, P7 stacks); no
    duration or magnitude changes.
  - **Recommended: A** — most expressive, mirrors weapons, and cleanly resolves
    AC3 (stacks = level). **OPEN QUESTION.**

- **Q3 — Scope of this work item.** Is this item **design + shared resolver +
  catalogue** (with per-power-up wiring/choice integration split into children),
  or full end-to-end (design + all wiring + hold-full integration) in one item?
  - A. Design + catalogue + pure resolver now; wiring/choice integration as
    children (matches AC4; smaller, reviewable changes).
  - B. Design/spec only; all implementation split into children.
  - C. Full end-to-end including hold-full choice integration in this item.

Add unit tests for the planned hybrid P9 Magnet behaviour in the EffectsRegistry before implementation (test-first).

# Docs: Update GDD §4.4 and README for hybrid P9 Magnet

**Summary:** Update all project documentation to reflect the hybrid P9 Magnet model — timed pickup, permanent stacking on upgrade.

**Headline:** Bring every player-facing description of the **P9 Magnet** into line with the P10 Mineral Scoop **hybrid model** — a **15 s, refresh-only** timed drop-attraction for field pickups and a **permanent stacking (cap 5)** attraction for the hold-full upgrade — updating GDD §4.4, its surrounding notes, the README shared-effects/power-up descriptions, and the `POWER_UP_CATALOGUE.P9` help copy, with a docs-guard test to stop the prose drifting from the code.

> Consolidated from the now-deleted duplicate **AH-0MUUM4MTA0081QSW** ("Docs: Update GDD §4.4 and README for hybrid P9 Magnet"); this item is the single surviving docs task and remains a child of the implementation epic **AH-0MUTOTLCY005NZ8L**.

## Problem statement

The P9 Magnet is documented everywhere as a **purely permanent** power-up ("permanent, passive"; "P9 permanent magnet stacks"), but the design has moved to a **hybrid** model identical to the P10 Mineral Scoop: timed on field pickup, permanent-stacking when chosen as a hold-full reward. The docs therefore describe behaviour the code is being changed to no longer have, and the two attraction power-ups are described inconsistently. Until the documentation is corrected the GDD is no longer a faithful design source and the README misleads both players and contributors.

## Users

- **Player / reader** — needs the GDD and README to describe what the magnet actually does: temporary convenience from a field drop, permanent escalating boon from a deliberate hold-full choice.
- **Developer / contributor** — needs one authoritative written description so the `POWER_UP_CATALOGUE.P9` help text, the GDD table/notes and the README cannot drift from the implemented hybrid semantics.

Example user stories:

- As a reader, after the magnet change I want the GDD §4.4 P9 row and notes to say "15 s timed pickup / permanent stacking when chosen as a reward (cap 5)", matching the P10 wording style, so the two attraction power-ups read consistently.
- As a new contributor, I want the README shared-effects description to state the hybrid P9 behaviour (timed field pickup, permanent stacks on upgrade) so I can understand the registry without reading `effects.ts`.
- As a maintainer, I want a docs-guard test that fails if the hybrid wording is removed or weakened, so the documentation cannot silently revert.

## Parent Acceptance Criteria Coverage

- [ ] **All related documentation is updated to reflect the changes, including code comments, README, and any relevant wiki or docs site entries.** Update GDD, README, and inline code comments; search for stale "P9 permanent" references.

## Acceptance Criteria

- [ ] **GDD §4.4 updated.** The P9 Magnet row in the GDD power-up table reads as a **hybrid** ("15 s timed pickup / permanent stacking when chosen as a reward (cap 5)"), matching the P10 row's wording style, and the P9 note(s) below the table are rewritten from "permanent, passive" to the hybrid model (timed field pickup refreshes, never stacks; hold-full upgrade is permanent, cap 5). The "tracked separately as AH-0MUTOTLCY005NZ8L and is out of scope here" line is removed now the change is delivered.
- [ ] **README updated.** The shared-effects / power-up descriptions in `README.md` (the `src/powerups/effects.ts` bullet and the P9 mentions in the gym sections) describe the hybrid P9 model consistently with P10.
- [ ] **Catalogue help copy updated.** `POWER_UP_CATALOGUE.P9.description` (`src/powerups/types.ts`) reads as the hybrid wording, matching the P10 description style.
- [ ] **Code comments updated.** Any inline comments referencing P9 as "permanent" (e.g. the `src/powerups/effects.ts` / `types.ts` header doc-comments) are updated to reflect the timed/permanent split.
- [ ] **Docs-guard test added.** A `src/magnetDocs.test.ts` docs guard (mirroring `src/aoeDocs.test.ts` / `src/weaponLevelingDocs.test.ts`) asserts the GDD §4.4 P9 row/notes and README contain the hybrid wording and that the P9 catalogue description matches, so the prose cannot silently drift.
- [ ] **No stale references remain.** A repo grep for the removed "P9 permanent" claims (e.g. "P9 permanent magnet stacks", "P9 Magnet … permanent, passive") returns only intentional/historical references.
- [ ] All related documentation is updated to reflect the changes, including code comments, README, and any relevant wiki or docs site entries.
- [ ] Full project test suite must pass with the new changes.

## Constraints

- **Documentation-only change.** No runtime behaviour is altered by this item; the implementation lives in AH-0MUTOTLCY005NZ8L and its children. If the implementation wording/semantics change during review, this brief's wording must follow the code, not lead it.
- **Parity rule (AGENTS.md):** shared behaviour lives once in `src/powerups/` + `src/scenes/core/`; the duplicate-body guard (`src/scenes/core/CombatScene.equivalence.test.ts`) and the gym-parity docs assertion stay green. This item must not weaken them.
- **Terminology lock:** field pickup = **15 s**, refresh-only, never stacks; hold-full upgrade = **permanent**, stacks up to **5**; single shared radius curve `magnetRadius(shipSize, stacks)` (base `1× ship size`, `+50%/stack`), same `MAGNET_ATTRACTION_SPEED` as P10. Do not introduce a new duration/cap.
- **CHANGELOG.md is excluded** (the ship skill owns it). Do not include CI/CD pipeline tests.

## Existing state

- `docs/Game Design Document.md` §4.4 describes P9 as **permanent, passive** in three places: the summary sentence (line ≈107), the table row (line ≈408, `*(permanent, passive)*`), and the note below the table (line ≈419). The P10 row/note already carry the hybrid wording to mirror, and the P10 note's closing line says the P9 consistency change "is tracked separately as AH-0MUTOTLCY005NZ8L and is out of scope here".
- `README.md` describes P9 as "P9 permanent magnet stacks (cap 5; …)" in the `src/powerups/effects.ts` bullet (line ≈616) and "P9 stacks" in the formation-gym bullet (line ≈633); the utility-gym section also lists P9 as a non-combat power-up.
- `src/powerups/types.ts` `POWER_UP_CATALOGUE.P9` has `description: 'Permanently pulls nearby drops toward the ship (stacks up to 5).'` and no `duration`, whereas P10 carries `duration: 15`.
- `src/powerups/effects.ts` still models P9 as permanent-only (`P9_MAX_STACKS = 5`, `_magnetStacks`, no `P9_MAGNET_DURATION`/`magnetEffectStacks()`), i.e. the implementation is **not yet done** — docs must follow it once complete.
- Docs-guard precedent exists: `src/aoeDocs.test.ts`, `src/weaponLevelingDocs.test.ts`, `src/vfx/endOfRunJuice.docs.test.ts` grep the GDD/README and cross-check code catalogues.

## Desired change

- **GDD §4.4:** rewrite the P9 summary mention, the P9 table row (label it *(hybrid: timed pickup / permanent upgrade)* like P10) and the P9 note to describe the hybrid model; remove the "tracked separately … out of scope here" sentence from the P10 note.
- **README:** update the `src/powerups/effects.ts` bullet and the formation-gym bullet (and any other P9-as-permanent phrasing) to the hybrid wording.
- **Catalogue:** update `POWER_UP_CATALOGUE.P9.description` (and add `duration: 15` if the implementation does) so help copy matches the docs.
- **Guard:** add `src/magnetDocs.test.ts` asserting the GDD §4.4 P9 row/notes and README contain the hybrid phrases and that the catalogue description matches, modelled on the existing docs-guard tests.
- **Inline comments:** update `src/powerups/effects.ts` / `types.ts` header doc-comments that call P9 "permanent" so code comments match the hybrid model.

## Key Files (predicted)

- `docs/Game Design Document.md` — §4.4 P9 summary sentence, table row, and note; P10 note closing sentence.
- `README.md` — `src/powerups/effects.ts` bullet, formation-gym bullet, utility-gym power-up list.
- `src/powerups/types.ts` — `POWER_UP_CATALOGUE.P9.description` (+ `duration`), header doc-comment.

- `src/magnetDocs.test.ts` — new docs-guard test (mirrors `src/aoeDocs.test.ts`).

## Risks and assumptions

- **Risk — documenting unimplemented behaviour.** The code change (AH-0MUTOTLCY005NZ8L children) may not be merged yet; the docs would then describe a future state. *Mitigation:* land the docs change alongside, or after, the implementation; treat the implementation as the source of truth for exact wording. See Open questions / dependency.
- **Risk — docs drift recurrence.** Nothing stops the prose reverting. *Mitigation:* the new docs-guard test fails on removal of the hybrid wording.
- **Risk — over-editing the GDD.** Many other sections mention P9 (rarity weights, cue table, history). *Mitigation:* scope the edit to the P9 permanent *claims*; leave rarity/weight/cue tables and historical intake records untouched unless they assert permanence.
- **Assumption:** the hybrid semantics (15 s timed / permanent cap-5 upgrade) are settled by the parent P10 intake and AH-0MUTOTLCY005NZ8L; no new interview is required to document them.
- **Assumption:** the P10 wording style is the canonical template for the P9 hybrid row.
- **Scope-creep risk:** a general documentation reorganisation, or new P10 docs guards, is out of scope; record extra opportunities as linked work items.

## Related work

- **AH-0MUTOTLCY005NZ8L — Make P9 Magnet timed on pickup and permanent-stack on upgrade** (in-progress, plan_complete): the implementation parent this docs change describes; contains the authoritative design decisions and the exact hybrid wording.

- `src/powerups/effects.ts`: added `P9_MAGNET_DURATION = 15`; the `MAGNET` case now branches on `permanent` (permanent -> +1 stack capped at `P9_MAX_STACKS`/5; field pickup -> 15 s refresh-only timed entry never incrementing stacks). Added `isMagnetActive()` and `magnetEffectStacks()` (permanent stacks when present, else 1 while timed, else 0); `activeEffects()` surfaces the timed P9 row plus the permanent `xN` stack row and never an `x0`; `reset()` clears both states.
- `src/scenes/core/CombatCoreScene.ts`: `_applyDropMagnet` now consumes `magnetEffectStacks()` so PlayScene and every gym pull drops with identical range semantics.
- `src/powerups/types.ts`: `POWER_UP_CATALOGUE.P9` gains `duration: 15` and the hybrid description ("Pulls nearby drops toward the ship - a 15 s pickup, or permanent stacking when chosen as a reward (cap 5).") matching P10 style.
- Tests: new hybrid P9 blocks in `src/powerups/effects.test.ts` (timed activation/expiry/refresh, permanent stacking/cap, `magnetEffectStacks()`, `activeEffects()` shape, `reset()`) plus a timed-row HUD case; migrated existing P9 field-pickup-as-permanent assertions to the permanent path in `HUD.test.ts`, `GymFormationScene.test.ts`, `GymPowerUpsUtility.test.ts` and `PlayScene.test.ts`.
- Docs: GDD §4.4 P9 row/notes rewritten to the hybrid model and the now-delivered "tracked separately" note removed; README `effects.ts`/gym descriptions updated; `GymPowerUpsUtility.ts` header comment updated.
- Parity: `_applyDropMagnet` remains shared in `CombatCoreScene`, so the duplicate-body/equivalence guard and `gymParityDocs.test.ts` stay green.
